title: Why an Object's Colour Changes How Heavy You Think It Is
hook: Ever notice how a black box feels heavier than a white one?

narration.text: Your brain can actually perceive objects of darker colours as being heavier.
This happens because darker colours visually absorb more light.
This absorption makes them seem more dense and compact to your eyes.
Your brain then translates this visual density into a feeling of increased weight.
You can test this right now with two identical objects painted differently.
Try lifting them and feel the subtle difference in perceived weight.
Try it right now and tell me if it worked on you in the comments, like this if it surprised you, and subscribe for more insights into your amazing mind.

description: It's not just your imagination; a darker object can genuinely feel heavier. This video explains the fascinating psychological effect behind why colour influences our perception of an object's weight. Prepare to have your mind blown!
topic: Why your perception of an object's weight can change depending on its colour. You can test this right now with two identical objects painted differently.
